title: The Most Common NDA Pitfall
summary: Discover how the right NDA protects your confidential data, limits AI vendor use, and helps you safeguard your intellectual property from the start.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


- Many NDAs focus on confidentiality without clearly restricting permitted use.
- Data shared with an AI vendor may raise additional questions about training, analytics, service improvement, and model enhancement.
- No-training restrictions should be considered alongside data processing agreements, product terms, ownership provisions, and other contractual language.
- Where personal data is involved, the GDPR's purpose limitation principle may also be relevant.
- The NDA should establish clear boundaries around how disclosed information may be used.


## Why NDAs Need More Than Confidentiality Protections


Most founders treat[NDAs](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/non-disclosure_agreement) as a tax, a burdensome formality to sign before getting to the "real" conversation. The assumption is simple: NDAs keep information secret. But that is the wrong focus. The most critical question isn't whether your information remains private; it’s whether the agreement actually controls how your information can be used once it leaves your hands.


This distinction is the source of significant, often silent, business risk. Many NDAs focus exclusively on[confidentiality](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/confidentiality_agreement) , the promise not to talk about what was shared, while remaining silent on **permitted use** . If you are sharing proprietary data to evaluate an AI vendor or a partnership, this gap matters. In practice, the risk depends heavily on the vendor’s architecture and whether your NDA interacts with broader data processing terms.


However, without an explicit restriction, data shared during a pilot, such as a proprietary customer dataset used to train a workflow prototype, can, in some cases, be incorporated into[model training pipelines](https://www.ftc.gov/policy/advocacy-research/tech-at-ftc/2024/01/ai-companies-uphold-your-privacy-confidentiality-commitments) , effectively turning your IP into the vendor's training set. The most effective NDAs do more than define confidential information; they establish clear boundaries around how disclosed data may be used.


## How Should an NDA Address Permitted Use and No-Training Restrictions?


To stop "boilerplate drift," we advise our clients to anchor the purpose of disclosure in the preamble; e.g., *'solely for the purpose of evaluating a potential commercial partnership regarding \[X\]';* and ensure the 'Permitted Use' section restricts the recipient to that narrow scope. While the logic is straightforward, the nuances of 'No-Training' language often determine whether your data remains segregated from a vendor's training environment. The challenge is that no-training restrictions rarely operate in isolation. Their effectiveness often depends on how they interact with data processing agreements, product terms, ownership provisions, and model-improvement clauses elsewhere in the contract.


Many vendor agreements contain broadly drafted data-use provisions that may permit analytics, service improvement, or model training activities beyond what customers initially expect. Because these issues often depend on a vendor's technical architecture and contractual framework, effective drafting requires more than inserting a standard no-training clause. Even well-drafted no-training provisions can be undermined by analytics, service-improvement, derivative works, or model-enhancement language elsewhere in the agreement.


## Why Vendor Data-Use Terms Matter


Ultimately, an NDA should be a bridge to a deal, not an unintended license to your intellectual property. If the text does not clearly define how your data is processed, the bridge is missing guardrails.


At[General Legal](https://general.legal/) , we help companies build commercial agreements that account for the realities of AI development, data governance, and model training. If you want to ensure your data rights are protected from day one, reach out for a review of your commercial agreements.


## FAQ


### Does an NDA only protect confidentiality, or does it also control how data is used?


An NDA can establish confidentiality obligations, but it may also need to address how disclosed information can be used. Permitted-use provisions can restrict a vendor from using the information for purposes beyond those agreed, including certain forms of model training or product improvement.


### What is a no-training restriction?


A no-training restriction is contractual language intended to prevent disclosed information from being used for model training. Its effectiveness depends on how it interacts with other provisions in the agreement.


### Can a vendor's other contractual terms affect a no-training restriction?


Yes. No-training restrictions rarely operate in isolation. Data processing agreements, product terms, ownership provisions, analytics provisions, service-improvement provisions, and model-enhancement clauses may all affect the practical scope of the restriction.


### Does GDPR matter when personal data is shared?


Where personal data is involved, GDPR requirements may be relevant. (Eur-Lex) Article 5 of the GDPR includes the purpose limitation principle, under which personal data is collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and should not be further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.


### What should a company review before sharing proprietary data with an AI vendor?


The company should consider the NDA's permitted-use provisions, no-training language, data processing agreements, product terms, ownership provisions, and other clauses addressing analytics, service improvement, derivative works, or model enhancement.
